admin_local_only: The hub listens only on this computer for now (listen is {listen}), so this address opens only here. To open it from a phone, change "listen" in {path} to ":{port}" (so the hub listens on every address) and run personad hub setup again.
admin_open_one: 2. Open this address {browser} and set an administrator password (the setup code is already in it, valid for {count} minute):
admin_open_other: 2. Open this address {browser} and set an administrator password (the setup code is already in it, valid for {count} minutes):
admin_set: 2. The administrator password is already set. The admin page is at:
browser_local: in a browser on this computer
browser_phone: in a browser on your phone
config_invalid_next: Fix the JSON and run again
config_kept: Using the existing {path}; values already in it stay as they are
config_unreadable: Can’t read {path}, or it isn’t a JSON object: {error}
config_unreadable_next: Fix or move this file, then run personad hub setup again
config_written_no_tls: Wrote {path} (plain HTTP port {port}; no LAN address found, so TLS stays off for now)
db_container_failed_next: If port {port} is taken or the image {image} can’t be pulled, deal with that and run again
db_container_unreachable: The database container is up, but can’t be reached: {error}
db_created: Created Postgres in Docker (container {container}, volume {volume}) and wrote its address into hub.json
db_existing: Using the existing Docker container {container}; wrote its address back into hub.json
db_password_unknown: The database container {container} exists, but hub.json doesn’t have its address and its password can’t be read
db_password_unknown_next: Write database_url back into hub.json (postgres://persona:<password>@127.0.0.1:{port}/persona?sslmode=disable), then run again
db_unreachable: Can’t connect to the database in hub.json: {error}
db_unreachable_next: Make sure Postgres is running and database_url is right, then run again
db_volume_failed_next: Read Docker’s error, deal with it and run again
docker_denied: Docker is here, but the current user isn’t allowed to use it
docker_denied_next: Run sudo usermod -aG docker {user}, sign out and back in, then run personad hub setup again
docker_logs_next: Run docker logs {container} to see why
docker_start_linux: Run sudo systemctl start docker, then run again
docker_start_mac: Open Docker Desktop or OrbStack, wait until it has started, then run again
docker_stopped: Docker is here, but it isn’t running
dropin_fix: To have it run {program}, change ExecStart in that drop-in (systemctl --user cat personad shows it), then run again
dropin_program: the service actually runs {program}: another drop-in changed its ExecStart
expired_hint: Once these expire, run personad hub setup again (finished steps aren’t redone), or personad hub pair for just a pairing code.
flag_json: one JSON object per line: {step, ok, detail, next} for each step, then {done, …}
flag_lang: the language to print in, and a new install’s initial user language: en, zh-Hans or ja (default: PERSONA_INSTALL_LANG, which install.sh sets, else the terminal’s language)
flag_listen: a new install’s plain HTTP port for the hub
flag_manager_service: for an existing hub: make the built-in manager a service of its own (a new install’s already is)
flag_no_service: install no background service (run personad hub run yourself); the hub starts the built-in manager itself
flag_outside: for use away from home too: the TLS port binds to every address, and the self-check looks at the internet as well
flag_tls: a new install’s TLS port for the hub (without an address, it binds to the LAN IPv4 address only)
flag_yes: ask nothing and take every default (including turning on linger with sudo)
health_next_journal: Run journalctl --user -u personad -n 50 to see the hub’s log
health_next_no_service: Run personad hub run in another terminal and, once it’s up, run personad hub setup --no-service again
health_ok: The hub is running and /api/v1/health passes on this machine
health_timeout_one: The hub didn’t answer on local port {port} within {count} second
health_timeout_other: The hub didn’t answer on local port {port} within {count} seconds
hub_unreachable: can’t reach the hub on this machine
journal_next: Run journalctl --user -u personad -n 50 to see why
kept_listen_note: {diffs}: --listen and --tls only shape a new install, and existing values stay as they are
lang_invalid: --lang must be en, zh-Hans or ja
launchctl_print_next: Run launchctl print {target} to see why
launchd_installed: Installed the background service (launchd {label}, starts when you log in); its log is in {path}
launchd_other_hub: The hub is already running, but not as a launchd service, so no background service was installed
launchd_other_hub_next: Stop the running hub and run personad hub setup again to install it as a service that starts when you log in
launchd_restarted: The background service is already installed; restarted it because {why} (launchd {label})
launchd_start_failed: Starting the existing launchd service {label} failed: {error}
launchd_unchanged: The background service is already installed and running, so it was left alone (launchd {label})
linger_ask: Keeping the hub running after you sign out and after a restart takes turning on linger with sudo (loginctl enable-linger). Turn it on now?
linger_manual: Run sudo loginctl enable-linger {user} so the hub keeps running after you sign out and after a restart
listen_flag_invalid: {address} isn’t a valid listen address: write :port or address:port
listen_no_port: listen in hub.json ({listen}) has no valid port
listen_no_port_next: Write it like ":18660" and run again
local_machine_added: Added this machine as a computer (kind: local)
local_machine_unknown: hub.json lists no computers, but which computers managers keep can’t be read ({error}), so this machine wasn’t added this time
local_machine_unknown_next: Check whether this computer is under Computers on the admin page and add it if not; once that’s fixed, run personad hub setup again
mac_stays: this Mac’s hub service ran personad before and still does (an installed Mac doesn’t move to persona-hub: Full Disk Access allows personad, and moving would need another entry there)
mac_switch: macOS Full Disk Access now looks at {program}: add it there if this machine’s node needs to read Desktop, Documents, Downloads or Messages
manager_back_to_child: to have the hub start it again: personad hub manager-mode child, then restart the hub’s service
manager_check_failed: Can’t install the built-in manager’s own service, so nothing was changed: {error}
manager_check_failed_next: Deal with what it says; if {bin} is too old, upgrade it first (run the install command again with --hub), then run personad hub setup --manager-service again
manager_child: The hub starts the built-in manager itself (assistant.mode child)
manager_child_next: To make it a service of its own (so it doesn’t restart whenever the hub restarts or updates): personad hub setup --manager-service
manager_code_failed: Couldn’t get a code to bind the built-in manager: {error}
manager_external: assistant.external in hub.json is true: the built-in manager runs elsewhere, and --manager-service leaves it alone
manager_external_next: To install its service on this machine, remove assistant.external from {path} first, then run again
manager_external_ok: assistant.external in hub.json: the built-in manager runs elsewhere, so it was left alone
manager_install_failed: The built-in manager’s own service wasn’t installed: {error}
manager_log_file: See the built-in manager’s log in {path}
manager_log_journal: Run journalctl --user -u {service} -n 50 to see the built-in manager’s log
manager_mode_unknown: assistant.mode in hub.json is {mode}, which the hub doesn’t know, so the built-in manager isn’t running
manager_mode_unknown_next: Change assistant.mode in {path} to service (or remove it so the hub starts the manager itself), then run again
manager_offline_one: The built-in manager’s service ({unit}) is installed but didn’t connect to the hub within {count} second
manager_offline_other: The built-in manager’s service ({unit}) is installed but didn’t connect to the hub within {count} seconds
manager_online: The built-in manager is a service of its own ({unit}), bound to this hub and connected
manager_retry: Deal with what it says, then run personad hub setup again; to use the built-in manager until then: personad hub manager-mode child, then restart the hub’s service so that it starts the manager itself
manager_retry_switched: Deal with what it says, then run personad hub setup --manager-service again
manager_service_conflict: --manager-service installs the built-in manager’s own service, so it can’t go with --no-service
manager_service_running: The built-in manager is a service of its own (assistant.mode service) and is running; left alone this time ({why})
manager_service_unattended: The built-in manager is a service of its own (assistant.mode service), but it wasn’t installed this time ({why}), so nothing runs it now
manager_service_unattended_next: Either keep it running yourself: get a code with personad hub manager-code, bind it with PERSONA_MANAGER_CODE=<code> personad manager join --builtin {url}, then keep PERSONA_ASSISTANT_DEPLOY=service {bin} assistant running; or run personad hub manager-mode child and restart the hub so that it starts the manager itself
manager_service_unavailable: The built-in manager’s own service can’t be installed here ({why})
no_arguments: hub setup takes no positional arguments
no_database: This computer has no database yet
no_database_next_linux: Install Docker (https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/), then run this command again
no_database_next_mac: Install Docker Desktop or OrbStack, then run this command again
no_docker_postgres: No Docker; there seems to be a Postgres on port 5432 of this computer
no_docker_postgres_next: Create a user persona and a database persona in it, write postgres://persona:<password>@127.0.0.1:5432/persona into database_url in {path}, then run again (docs/server/server.md “Database”); or install Docker and run again
no_linger: linger isn’t on: the hub stops when you sign out
no_systemd: This computer has no systemd user services (systemctl --user doesn’t work)
no_systemd_next: Run again with --no-service and keep {bin} hub running yourself (with tmux or nohup, for example)
note_manager_service: assistant.mode is now service: the hub no longer starts the built-in manager, which runs as a service of its own
pair_code_failed: The hub is running, but no pairing code came back: {error}
pair_code_failed_next: Run personad hub pair and try again
pair_link: If you can’t scan it, send this pairing link to your phone and open it there: {url}
pair_qr_one: 1. Scan this QR code with the Persona app to pair your phone (valid for {count} minute):
pair_qr_other: 1. Scan this QR code with the Persona app to pair your phone (valid for {count} minutes):
ports_busy_next: Stop the program holding it, or change listen / public.tls_listen in {path}, then run again
ports_busy_one: Port {ports} is taken by another program, perhaps another Persona
ports_busy_other: Ports {ports} are taken by another program, perhaps another Persona
ports_moved: ports {listen} / {tls} are taken by another program, perhaps another Persona, so this uses {new_listen} / {new_tls}
restart_why_binary: the hub has a new version
restart_why_manager_service: the built-in manager became a service of its own
service_ready: The background service is already installed
service_restarted_hub: The background service is already installed; restarted the hub because {why}
service_unchanged: The background service is already installed and running, so it was left alone
service_unsupported: Background services can’t be installed on {os} yet
service_unsupported_next: Add --no-service and keep personad hub run running yourself
service_updated: The background service is already installed; the hub has a new version, so it was restarted
setup_code_failed: The hub is running, but no setup code for the admin page came back: {error}
setup_code_failed_next: Run personad hub admin setup-code and try again
split_skipped: persona-hub wasn’t used ({why}), so the service runs personad
switched_child: the service now runs {program}; the built-in manager restarted with it
switched_restarted: the service now runs {program}; restarted the hub
switched_restarted_child: the service now runs {program}; restarted the hub, and the built-in manager restarted with it
switched_restarted_it: the service now runs {program} and was restarted
systemd_installed: Installed and started the background service (systemd user service personad)
systemd_installed_socket: Installed and started the background service (systemd user service personad, with its ports held by personad.socket)
title: Setting up the hub (personad hub setup)
undo_done: assistant.mode is changed back, and the hub starts the built-in manager itself as before
undo_failed: assistant.mode wasn’t changed back ({error}): run personad hub manager-mode child, then restart the hub’s service
undo_restart_failed: assistant.mode is changed back, but restarting the hub failed ({error}): the hub starts the built-in manager itself only once its service restarts
undo_restarted: changed back to the hub starting the built-in manager itself, and restarted the hub
